state: Challenge a proposed Can-native test system using existing source, without implementing or running experiments. Can is authored by AI agents; unrestricted ordinary Can functions must own scenarios, expectations, scheduling and reports, and authored foreign host harnesses must be eliminated. The selected backend is full Can compiled to TypeScript/Bun. Qualified reference toolchain R builds trusted Can judges; candidate C is only a subject; native Go owner N supervises disposable workers and resources externally. All work is bounded on a 256 GB MacBook, cleanup is registered before effects, and no persistent full bundles/private caches are allowed. Current native.ts and delegated runtime tests need exact JSON source lexemes, int64 beyond safe JS numbers, negative-zero bits, Proxy/getter/revocation, zero thenable accesses, object/occurrence identity and late diagnostics/resource use. The catalogue is closed and typed. Ordinary named Can callables emit async Promise<Completion<T>> closures; completion.ts has value/invokeSync for specific synchronous paths, which does not prove arbitrary Can callback support for synchronous JS traps. Raw hostile values cannot be returned through async transport without risking assimilation; use inert scoped handles and tagged facts. RunOutput validates runtime manifest identity and private module hashes, so R-built probes cannot silently swap C runtime imports. Raw Bun facts, R-built observers and C production-adapter behavior are distinct; C code must never enter the trusted judge. Fixed immediate native descriptor actions can model common getter/trap faults without a scenario language, but presenting those hostile values to a C adapter in the same realm remains unqualified. Browser grid.mjs pauses requests, delays delivery, fetches upstream then corrupts only returned bytes, retries the same operation ID and collects asynchronous callback failures. Proposed browser bindings give Can paused request tokens, separate upstream fetch/delivery, at-most-once resolution, bounded event streams and final seal; no JS-source eval. Controller round trips and callback draining have not been qualified. Current SQL F02/F03 drivers call Can SQL runtime adapters and separately issue raw Bun SQL. They exercise lock contention, SKIP LOCKED, NOWAIT/55P03, transaction poisoning/25P02 and replay, RETURNING/cardinality, exact int64/money/time/JSON, eight/16 concurrent writers and optional MySQL plus SQLite variants. Their raw-driver independence is from Can's adapter, not Bun SQL. A new raw observer must retain connection/transaction identity, exact values, native errors and ambiguous-commit facts without retry; a flat pooled query API is insufficient for session-scoped checks. Product-launcher tests intentionally pass hostile BUN_OPTIONS/NODE_OPTIONS to C's Go CLI, which should sanitize child Bun startup and deliver original application data on fd 3. N must preserve those inputs to C while isolating R/N; direct entry launches use sanitized startup plus fd 3 EOF, binary stdin and an fd 4 generation lease. EOF/backpressure, non-reading children and lease survival after launcher exit require small later checks. Source review is not proof that bindings work. Retained migration obligations need their own Can checks, negative controls and cleanup evidence; passing a mechanism experiment cannot retire a harness. Additional browser source constraints: interception must progress while the initiating click is outstanding, and two DOM clicks in one synchronous page task are not equivalent to two remote calls. Fixed typed action batches, clone/append node identity, listener registration order and defaultPrevented, page-origin Fetch under real credentials/CSP, and Can-owned browser codec vectors are missing or unqualified bindings. These are mechanics, not permission for scripted scenarios. Remote Firefox is a shared server: dispose the owned context/connection only. Additional SQL findings: F02 lock evidence comes from runtime actors rather than a raw independent lock oracle. F03's comment that RETURNING is future is stale against current checker/runtime support. Its poisoned transaction has no successful pre-poison write, so adding a sentinel and a later raw read strengthens the rollback oracle rather than describing existing coverage. SQL operation deadlines do not cancel native work; after commit_unknown, wait for known settlement and fence new activity before interpreting a fresh independent read, otherwise preserve uncertainty. The old cold-pool workaround is not evidence against a later callback-binding fix. Fixed table names and swallowed cleanup errors in old drivers cannot establish safe namespace ownership.

native_bridge_priority.instructions: Which next design commitment best addresses the native-value and callback evidence while preserving the agreed full-Can scope?

criteria.explicit_bridge: Keep the backend and separate provenance roles; first qualify handles, immediate native descriptors and explicit same-realm C adapter ingress. Treat richer synchronous Can callback support as a separately gated binding, while ordinary Can helpers remain unrestricted.
criteria.general_sync_first: Prioritize a general checked synchronous Can callback companion before migrating hostile native cases, so accessor/trap logic can be authored in Can; retain native descriptors only for irreducible raw constructors.
criteria.interpreter_first: Reopen the backend choice now and prototype a checked-IR interpreter with direct synchronous native bindings before committing the native migration, retaining the external owner and full Can semantics.

browser_control_location.instructions: Where should the asynchronous interception decision execute first, given the existing corruption/replay cases and unqualified round trip?

criteria.tokens_to_can: Keep decisions in the Can worker using paused route tokens, one-shot upstream and delivery actions and a complete event seal; test this rendezvous before adding locally compiled route callbacks.
criteria.local_can_callback: Compile ordinary R-built Can route callbacks into the isolated browser-driver service first, avoiding decision round trips while returning raw observations to the separate Can judge.
criteria.both_initially: Require both worker token decisions and driver-local compiled Can callbacks in the first browser capability release, selecting between them by each case's timing needs.

database_observer.instructions: Which independent SQL observation strategy is proportionate to the current protected boundary?

criteria.raw_driver_scoped: Use generic direct-driver operations with separate pinned connection/transaction handles and lossless native facts; claim independence from the Can SQL adapter only, requiring another driver when an obligation targets Bun SQL itself.
criteria.cli_default: Adopt psql/MySQL/SQLite command-line clients as the default observer, defining framed session transport and exact output parsing even for checks aimed only at the Can adapter.
criteria.dual_every_case: Require both raw Bun SQL and a separate native client/driver for every SQL case, comparing two observation streams before crediting adapter coverage.
